newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Santos sees further profit growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Santos sees further profit growth.

text.p: Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd expects further profit growth over 1998 and 1999 as production increases, managing director Ross Adler said on Tuesday.
"Subject to the usual qualifications, we expect increased production in 1998 and 1999 to translate into further growth in earnings," Adler told a luncheon in Melbourne.
In a speech outlining the company's strategy over the next decade, Adler said the company's traditional gas business would remain very important but liquid production would begin to rise from 1998.
"Reflecting this, I expect that offshore Australia will be a well-established area of interest a decade from now," he said.
"Not only will East Spar and Stag be producing, but also Bayu-Undan and I hope other projects," he said.

Santos surprised the market with a 40 percent rise in net profit to A$195.1 million in calendar 1996. In the first quarter of 1997, sales revenue rose 22.5 percent from a year earlier to A$181.3 million while production volume rose 6.8 percent to 9.6 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe).
Adler said he expected Santos gas production to grow solidly over the next decade with more output coming from offshore.
"A decade hence the South Australian Cooper Basin is still likely to be an important source of gas for New South Wales and South Australia," Adler said.
He said he expected Queensland would be a mature part of its gas business, selling considerable more gas than it does today.

"I expect that we will be selling gas from the Northern Territory to southern and eastern states," he said. He added the group also wanted to be a meaningful player in the Western Australian gas industry.

Adler said the lift in offshore production would come from the East Spar and Stag projects both offshore Western Australia and the Bayu-Undan gas condensate field in the zone of co-operation between Australia and Indonesia in the Timor Sea.
In January, Santos completed the purchase of interests in the Southeast Gobe field in Papua New Guinea (PNG).

"...If we are successful in PNG, it is possible to envisage another oil production project or projects within the next 10 years," Adler said. He said he expected the group's British and U.S. operations to be larger than they are currently.
"In short, if we are successful, Santos will have developed from being heavily reliant on the Cooper Basin to having multiple areas of interest, generating continuous growth," Adler said.
"The next two-three years are critical in turning this vision into reality and I believe we have a good chance of being successful," he said.
